\section{Overview}

Declarations of the Lean module \texttt{FABL.Chapter07.HastadTests}.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Sign predicate]
\lean{FABL.SignPredicate}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p191-b002}
\label{FABL.SignPredicate}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.Sign}
A sign predicate consists of an arity $k\in\mathbb N$ and a Boolean-valued acceptance
rule on $k$ signs; that is, a function from sign-valued $k$-tuples to
$\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Sign query check]
\lean{FABL.SignQueryCheck}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p191-b002}
\label{FABL.SignQueryCheck}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.SignPredicate}
For $n\in\mathbb N$, a sign query check consists of a sign predicate of arity $k$ and an
assignment of an $n$-dimensional sign-cube point to each of its $k$ input positions.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Sign tester]
\lean{FABL.SignTester}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p174-b001,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p191-b002
}
\label{FABL.SignTester}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.SignQueryCheck}
For $n\in\mathbb N$, a sign tester consists of a finite seed space equipped with a
probability distribution and a rule assigning a sign query check on the $n$-dimensional
sign cube to each seed.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Bounded cube function]
\lean{FABL.BoundedCubeFunction}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p199-b006}
\label{FABL.BoundedCubeFunction}
\leanok
For $n\in\mathbb N$, a bounded cube function is a real-valued function on the
$n$-dimensional sign cube whose values all lie in $[-1,1]$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Real-valued form of a Boolean function]
\lean{FABL.BoundedCubeFunction.ofBoolean}
\label{FABL.BoundedCubeFunction.ofBoolean}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.BoundedCubeFunction}
For a Boolean function $f$ on the $n$-dimensional sign cube, regard its values as real
numbers via the sign-to-real identification. This defines a real-valued function whose
values all lie in $[-1,1]$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Sign distribution with prescribed mean]
\lean{FABL.signPMFOfMean}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p199-b006}
\label{FABL.signPMFOfMean}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.Sign, FABL.coordinateNoisePMF}
For a real number $\mu\in[-1,1]$, the sign distribution with mean parameter $\mu$ is the
one-coordinate noise probability mass function with parameter $\mu$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Mean of a sign distribution]
\lean{FABL.pmfExpectation_signPMFOfMean}
\label{FABL.pmfExpectation_signPMFOfMean}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.pmfExpectation, FABL.pmfExpectation_coordinateNoisePMF_signValue, FABL.signPMFOfMean, FABL.signValue}
\difficulty{3}
Let $\mu\in[-1,1]$. For a random sign in $\{\pm1\}$ that equals $1$ with probability
$(1+\mu)/2$ and $-1$ otherwise, its expected value is $\mu$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Randomized acceptance value]
\lean{FABL.SignPredicate.randomizedValue}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p199-b003,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p199-b006
}
\label{FABL.SignPredicate.randomizedValue}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.SignPredicate, FABL.independentProductPMF, FABL.pmfExpectation, FABL.signPMFOfMean}
Let $P$ be a sign predicate of arity $k$, and assign each input position $i$ a mean
parameter $\mu_i\in[-1,1]$. Sample the $k$ signs independently, with the sign at
position $i$ drawn from the sign distribution of mean $\mu_i$, and evaluate the
probability that $P$ accepts the resulting tuple.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Randomized value of a sign query check]
\lean{FABL.SignQueryCheck.randomizedValue}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p199-b006}
\label{FABL.SignQueryCheck.randomizedValue}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BoundedCubeFunction, FABL.SignPredicate.randomizedValue, FABL.SignQueryCheck}
Let $C$ be a check consisting of a sign predicate and a Boolean-cube query for each
input position, and let $f$ be a real-valued function on the Boolean cube whose values
lie in $[-1,1]$. Its randomized value is the probability that the predicate accepts when
each query is independently replaced by a random sign with mean equal to the value of
$f$ on that query.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Acceptance value of a sign tester]
\lean{FABL.SignTester.acceptanceProbability}
\label{FABL.SignTester.acceptanceProbability}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BoundedCubeFunction, FABL.SignQueryCheck.randomizedValue, FABL.SignTester, FABL.pmfExpectation}
Let $T$ be a randomized sign tester with a finite seed space and a probability law on
that space, and let $f$ be a real-valued function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube
taking values in $[-1,1]$. Its acceptance probability is the expected randomized value
of the check selected by the sampled seed, evaluated on $f$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Tester uses only allowed predicates]
\lean{FABL.SignTester.UsesPredicates}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p191-b002}
\label{FABL.SignTester.UsesPredicates}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.SignPredicate, FABL.SignTester}
Let $T$ be a tester with a finite seed space and a probability law on its seeds, and let
$\Psi$ be a set of sign predicates. The tester uses only predicates in $\Psi$ if, for
every seed, the predicate in the check selected by that seed belongs to $\Psi$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Dictator versus no-notables test]
\lean{FABL.IsDictatorVsNoNotablesTest}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p191-b002}
\label{FABL.IsDictatorVsNoNotablesTest}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BoundedCubeFunction, FABL.BoundedCubeFunction.ofBoolean, FABL.HasSmallStableInfluences, FABL.SignPredicate, FABL.SignTester, FABL.SignTester.UsesPredicates, FABL.SignTester.acceptanceProbability, FABL.dictator}
Let $\Psi$ be a finite set of sign predicates, let $\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb R$ satisfy
$0<\alpha<\beta\le1$, and let $e\colon\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ map $[0,1]$ into $[0,1]$
and tend to $0$ as its argument tends to $0$ through positive values. Suppose a tester
is specified for every positive dimension, uses only predicates in $\Psi$, accepts every
coordinate dictator with probability at least $\beta$, and accepts every function with
no $(\varepsilon,\varepsilon)$-notable coordinate with probability at most
$\alpha+e(\varepsilon)$ for every $\varepsilon\in[0,1]$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Three-variable linear sign predicate]
\lean{FABL.e3LinPredicate}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p184-b003,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p185-b002,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p185-b003
}
\label{FABL.e3LinPredicate}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.Sign, FABL.SignPredicate}
For a sign $b\in\{\pm1\}$, define a predicate on three signs that accepts
$(y_0,y_1,y_2)$ exactly when $y_0y_1y_2=b$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Indicator formula for a three-sign equation]
\lean{FABL.e3LinPredicate_indicator_eq}
\label{FABL.e3LinPredicate_indicator_eq}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.Sign, FABL.e3LinPredicate, FABL.signValue}
\difficulty{4}
For a sign $b$ and three signs $y_0,y_1,y_2$, the indicator that $y_0y_1y_2=b$ equals
$\bigl(1+b\,y_0y_1y_2\bigr)/2$, identifying each sign with its real value.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Three-variable linear sign predicates]
\lean{FABL.maxE3LinPredicates}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p184-b003,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p185-b002
}
\label{FABL.maxE3LinPredicates}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.SignPredicate, FABL.e3LinPredicate}
Let $\mathcal P$ be the set of all predicates on three signs that accept exactly when
the product of the three input signs equals a fixed sign $b\in\{\pm1\}$, as $b$ ranges
over $\{\pm1\}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Finiteness of linear predicates]
\lean{FABL.maxE3LinPredicates_finite}
\label{FABL.maxE3LinPredicates_finite}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.e3LinPredicate, FABL.maxE3LinPredicates}
\difficulty{1}
For each finite arity bound, the family of maximum E3 linear predicates is finite.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Scaled pointwise product of sign vectors]
\lean{FABL.scaledPointwiseProduct}
\label{FABL.scaledPointwiseProduct}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.Sign}
For a sign $b$ and sign vectors $x,y$ on $n$ coordinates, define their scaled pointwise
product to be the sign vector whose $i$th coordinate is $b x_i y_i$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Monomial of a scaled pointwise product]
\lean{FABL.monomial_scaledPointwiseProduct}
\label{FABL.monomial_scaledPointwiseProduct}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.Sign, FABL.monomial, FABL.scaledPointwiseProduct, FABL.signValue}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $b$ be a sign, let $x$ and $y$ be vectors of $n$ signs,
and let $S$ be a subset of the coordinate indices. The monomial indexed by $S$ at the
vector with coordinates $b x_i y_i$ equals the sign value of $b$ raised to $|S|$, times
the monomial indexed by $S$ at $x$, times the monomial indexed by $S$ at $y$.
\end{theorem}

  {Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}
  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p014-b002,
    pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p022-b001}
For every $n\in\mathbb N$, real parameter $\rho$, function $f:\{−1,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$,
and sign $b\in\{−1,1\}$, the uniform expectation over independent uniform
$x,y\in\{−1,1\}^n$ of $f(x)f(y)$ times the noise operator applied to $f$ at the point
whose $i$th coordinate is $b x_i y_i$ equals $\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}
b^{|S|}\rho^{|S|}\widehat f(S)^3$, where $\widehat f(S)$ is the uniform Fourier
coefficient of $f$ at $S$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Håstad tester seed]
\lean{FABL.HastadSeed}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p194-b003}
\label{FABL.HastadSeed}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.Sign}
For a natural number $n$, a Håstad tester seed consists of two sign vectors
$x,y\in\{\pm1\}^n$, a sign $b\in\{\pm1\}$, and a sign vector $z\in\{\pm1\}^n$
representing the noisy version of the coordinatewise product $bxy$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Håstad seed distribution]
\lean{FABL.hastadSeedPMF}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p194-b003}
\label{FABL.hastadSeedPMF}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.HastadSeed, FABL.Sign, FABL.noiseKernel, FABL.scaledPointwiseProduct, FABL.uniformPMF}
Let $n$ be a natural number and let $\delta\in[0,1]$. Choose $x$ and $y$ independently
and uniformly from $\{\pm1\}^n$, and choose $b$ uniformly from $\{\pm1\}$. Then draw $z$
from the noise kernel with parameter $1-\delta$, applied to the vector whose coordinates
are $b x_i y_i$, and return $(x,y,b,z)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Håstad tester]
\lean{FABL.hastadTester}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p194-b003}
\label{FABL.hastadTester}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.HastadSeed, FABL.SignTester, FABL.e3LinPredicate, FABL.hastadSeedPMF}
Let $n$ be a natural number and let $\delta\in[0,1]$. Define a tester whose random seed
has the Håstad seed distribution with parameter $\delta$; on seed $(x,y,b,z)$, its check
uses the predicate that accepts three signs exactly when their product is $b$, and
queries the vectors $x,y,z$ in that order.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Håstad tester acceptance probability]
\lean{FABL.hastadAcceptanceProbability}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p194-b003}
\label{FABL.hastadAcceptanceProbability}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BoundedCubeFunction, FABL.SignTester.acceptanceProbability, FABL.hastadTester}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $␀$ be a real number in $[0,1]$, and let $f$ be a
real-valued function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube whose values lie in $[-1,1]$. The
Håstad tester with parameter $␀$ has an acceptance probability on input function $f$,
which defines a real number.
\end{definition}

  {FABL.hastadAcceptanceProbability}
  {context}
  {Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}
  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p194-b003,
    pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p199-b006}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $0\leq\delta\leq1$, and let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to[-1,1]$.
The acceptance probability of the Håstad tester with noise parameter $\delta$ equals the
expectation, over independent uniform $x,y\in\{-1,1\}^n$ and a uniform sign
$b\in\{-1,1\}$, of $\frac{1+b f(x)f(y)(T_{1-\delta}f)(bxy)}{2}$, where $bxy$ is the
coordinatewise product and $T_{1-\delta}$ is the noise operator with parameter
$1-\delta$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Moment of a uniform random sign]
\lean{FABL.expect_signValue_pow_succ}
\label{FABL.expect_signValue_pow_succ}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.Sign, FABL.expect_signValue_eq_zero, FABL.signValue}
\difficulty{4}
Let $b$ be uniform on $\\{-1,1\}$, and let $k$ be a nonnegative integer. Then
$\\mathbb{E}[b^{k+1}]$ is $1$ if $k$ is odd and $0$ if $k$ is even.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Affine rule for iterated finite averages]
\lean{FABL.expect_expect_affine}
\label{FABL.expect_expect_affine}
\leanok
\difficulty{3}
Let $X$ and $Y$ be finite nonempty sets, let $c,d\in\mathbb R$, and let $g:X\times
Y\to\mathbb R$. The uniform average over $x\in X$ of the uniform average over $y\in Y$
of $c+d g(x,y)$ equals $c+d$ times the corresponding iterated uniform average of
$g(x,y)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[A sign moment with a power]
\lean{FABL.expect_signValue_mul_power}
\label{FABL.expect_signValue_mul_power}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.Sign, FABL.expect_signValue_pow_succ, FABL.signValue}
\difficulty{3}
For every nonnegative integer $k$ and every real number $c$, the uniform mean over
$b\in\{−1,1\}$ of $b(b^k c)$ equals $c$ if $k$ is odd and $0$ if $k$ is even.
\end{theorem}

\proofstep
  {FABL.expect_signValue_mul_power}
  {context}
  {Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}
  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p024-b007,
    pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p025-b001}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $0\leq\delta\leq1$, and let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to[-1,1]$.
Its Håstad tester acceptance probability with noise parameter $\delta$ is
$\frac12+\frac12\sum_{S\subseteq[n],\,|S|\text{ odd}}(1-\delta)^{|S|}\widehat f(S)^3$,
where $\widehat f(S)=\mathbb E_x[f(x)\prod_{i\in S}x_i]$ for uniform $x\in\{-1,1\}^n$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Odd BLR tester]
\lean{FABL.oddBLRTester}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p193-b003}
\label{FABL.oddBLRTester}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.SignTester, FABL.hastadTester}
For each nonnegative integer $n$, define the odd BLR tester to be the Håstad tester on
the $n$-dimensional sign cube with parameter $0$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Odd BLR acceptance probability]
\lean{FABL.oddBLRAcceptanceProbability}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p193-b003}
\label{FABL.oddBLRAcceptanceProbability}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BoundedCubeFunction, FABL.SignTester.acceptanceProbability, FABL.oddBLRTester}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and let $f$ be a real-valued function on the
$n$-dimensional sign cube whose values lie in $[-1,1]$. The odd BLR tester's acceptance
probability on $f$ defines a real number.
\end{definition}

    pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p193-b004}
Let $n$ be a natural number and let $f$ map the sign cube $\\{-1,1\\}^n$ to $\\{ -1,1
\\}$. The acceptance probability of the odd BLR test on $f$ is
$\\frac12+\\frac12\\sum_{S\\subseteq[n],\,|S|\\text{ odd}}\\widehat f(S)^3$, where
$\\widehat f(S)$ is the Fourier coefficient of $f$ at $S$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Odd-cardinality Fourier frequencies]
\lean{FABL.oddFourierFrequencies}
\label{FABL.oddFourierFrequencies}
\leanok
For a positive integer $n$, the odd Fourier frequencies are the subsets of
$\{1,\\ldots,n\\}$ having odd cardinality.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Nonempty odd Fourier frequencies]
\lean{FABL.oddFourierFrequencies_nonempty}
\label{FABL.oddFourierFrequencies_nonempty}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.oddFourierFrequencies}
\difficulty{1}
For every positive natural number $n$, there is an odd-cardinality subset of
${0,1,ots,n-1}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Maximum odd Fourier coefficient]
\lean{FABL.oddFourierMaximum}
\label{FABL.oddFourierMaximum}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.fourierCoeff, FABL.oddFourierFrequencies, FABL.oddFourierFrequencies_nonempty}
Let $n>0$ and let $f$ be a Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube. Its odd
Fourier maximum is the largest Fourier coefficient, in the real-valued sign
representation of $f$, among the frequencies indexed by subsets of odd cardinality.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Maximum odd Fourier coefficient]
\lean{FABL.nonnegativeOddFourierMaximum}
\label{FABL.nonnegativeOddFourierMaximum}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.fourierCoeff, FABL.oddFourierFrequencies}
Let $f$ be a sign-valued function on the $n$-dimensional Boolean cube. Its nonnegative
odd Fourier maximum is the largest of $0$ and the Fourier coefficients of $f$, viewed as
real-valued, indexed by odd-cardinality frequencies.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Nonnegative odd Fourier maximum]
\lean{FABL.nonnegativeOddFourierMaximum_eq_max}
\label{FABL.nonnegativeOddFourierMaximum_eq_max}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.nonnegativeOddFourierMaximum, FABL.oddFourierMaximum}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a positive integer and let $f$ be a function from the $n$-dimensional Boolean
cube to the signs. The maximum of zero and the largest Fourier coefficient of $f$
indexed by an odd-cardinality subset equals the nonnegative odd Fourier maximum of $f$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Nonnegativity of the odd Fourier maximum]
\lean{FABL.nonnegativeOddFourierMaximum_zero_le}
\label{FABL.nonnegativeOddFourierMaximum_zero_le}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.fourierCoeff, FABL.nonnegativeOddFourierMaximum, FABL.oddFourierFrequencies}
\difficulty{2}
For every nonnegative integer $n$ and every function $f$ from the $n$-dimensional
Boolean cube to the signs, the nonnegative odd Fourier maximum of $f$ is nonnegative.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Odd Fourier coefficients bounded by their maximum]
\lean{FABL.fourierCoeff_le_nonnegativeOddFourierMaximum}
\label{FABL.fourierCoeff_le_nonnegativeOddFourierMaximum}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.fourierCoeff, FABL.nonnegativeOddFourierMaximum, FABL.oddFourierFrequencies}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and let $f:\{\pm1\}^n\to\{\pm1\}$. For every subset $S$
of the coordinates with odd cardinality, the Fourier coefficient of $f$ at $S$ is at
most the maximum of $0$ and all Fourier coefficients at odd-cardinality subsets of the
coordinates.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Odd Fourier maximum in dimension zero]
\lean{FABL.nonnegativeOddFourierMaximum_dimension_zero}
\label{FABL.nonnegativeOddFourierMaximum_dimension_zero}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.nonnegativeOddFourierMaximum, FABL.oddFourierFrequencies}
\difficulty{4}
For every function from the zero-dimensional Boolean cube to the signs, the maximum of
zero and its Fourier coefficients indexed by odd-cardinality subsets is zero.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Odd BLR Corrected Fourier Maximum Bound]
\lean{FABL.oddBLRAcceptanceProbability_le_correctedMaximum}
\label{FABL.oddBLRAcceptanceProbability_le_correctedMaximum}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.BoundedCubeFunction.ofBoolean, FABL.fourierCoeff, FABL.fourierCoeff_le_nonnegativeOddFourierMaximum, FABL.nonnegativeOddFourierMaximum, FABL.nonnegativeOddFourierMaximum_zero_le, FABL.oddBLRAcceptanceProbability, FABL.oddBLRAcceptanceProbability_eq_fourierSum, FABL.sum_sq_fourierCoeff_eq_one}
\difficulty{5}
Let $n$ be a natural number and let $f$ map the sign cube $\\{-1,1\\}^n$ to
$\\{-1,1\\}$. The odd BLR acceptance probability is at most $\\frac12+\\frac12 M$, where
$M$ is the maximum of $0$ and the Fourier coefficients $\\widehat f(S)$ over all
odd-cardinality subsets $S\\subseteq[n]$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Negated OR function]
\lean{FABL.oddBLRBookBoundCounterexample}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p193-b004}
\label{FABL.oddBLRBookBoundCounterexample}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.orFunction}
On the two-dimensional sign cube, define a Boolean function by taking the pointwise
negation of the OR function.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Real form of the counterexample]
\lean{FABL.oddBLRBookBoundCounterexample_toReal}
\label{FABL.oddBLRBookBoundCounterexample_toReal}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.Sign, FABL.monomial, FABL.oddBLRBookBoundCounterexample, FABL.orFunction, FABL.signValue}
\difficulty{5}
For every point $x$ of the two-dimensional sign cube, the real-valued form of the
negative OR function equals $\bigl(1- x_0-x_1-x_0x_1\bigr)/2$, where $x_0$ and $x_1$ are
the coordinate signs of $x$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Fourier coefficients of the odd BLR counterexample]
\lean{FABL.fourierCoeff_oddBLRBookBoundCounterexample}
\label{FABL.fourierCoeff_oddBLRBookBoundCounterexample}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.SignCube, FABL.expect_monomial, FABL.expect_monomial_mul, FABL.fourierCoeff, FABL.monomial, FABL.oddBLRBookBoundCounterexample, FABL.oddBLRBookBoundCounterexample_toReal}
\difficulty{4}
Let $T$ be any subset of $\{0,1\}$. For the fixed Boolean function on the
two-dimensional sign cube used as a counterexample to the odd BLR book bound, its
Fourier coefficient at $T$ equals one half of the indicator that $T$ is empty, minus one
half for each of the three nonempty subsets $\{0\}$, $\{1\}$, and $\{0,1\}$ that equals
$T$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Coefficient at the first coordinate]
\lean{FABL.fourierCoeff_oddBLRBookBoundCounterexample_zero}
\label{FABL.fourierCoeff_oddBLRBookBoundCounterexample_zero}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.fourierCoeff, FABL.fourierCoeff_oddBLRBookBoundCounterexample, FABL.oddBLRBookBoundCounterexample}
\difficulty{4}
For the fixed Boolean function on the two-dimensional sign cube used as a counterexample
to the odd BLR book bound, the Fourier coefficient at the singleton coordinate set
$\{0\}$ is $-1/2$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Coefficient at the second coordinate]
\lean{FABL.fourierCoeff_oddBLRBookBoundCounterexample_one}
\label{FABL.fourierCoeff_oddBLRBookBoundCounterexample_one}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.fourierCoeff, FABL.fourierCoeff_oddBLRBookBoundCounterexample, FABL.oddBLRBookBoundCounterexample}
\difficulty{4}
For the fixed Boolean function on the two-dimensional sign cube used as a counterexample
to the odd BLR book bound, the Fourier coefficient at the singleton coordinate set
$\{1\}$ is $-1/2$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Odd frequencies in dimension two]
\lean{FABL.oddFourierFrequencies_two}
\label{FABL.oddFourierFrequencies_two}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.oddFourierFrequencies}
\difficulty{1}
The odd-cardinality subsets of ${0,1}$ are exactly ${0}$ and ${1}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Odd Fourier maximum of the counterexample]
\lean{FABL.oddBLRBookBoundCounterexample_oddMaximum}
\label{FABL.oddBLRBookBoundCounterexample_oddMaximum}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.fourierCoeff_oddBLRBookBoundCounterexample_one, FABL.fourierCoeff_oddBLRBookBoundCounterexample_zero, FABL.oddBLRBookBoundCounterexample, FABL.oddFourierFrequencies_two, FABL.oddFourierMaximum}
\difficulty{1}
For the function on the two-dimensional sign cube that is the negative of the OR
function, the maximum of its Fourier coefficients over all odd-cardinality frequencies

\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Printed bound for the counterexample]
\lean{FABL.oddBLRBookBoundCounterexample_printed_rhs}
\label{FABL.oddBLRBookBoundCounterexample_printed_rhs}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.oddBLRBookBoundCounterexample, FABL.oddBLRBookBoundCounterexample_oddMaximum, FABL.oddFourierMaximum}
\difficulty{2}
For the negative of the OR function on the two-dimensional sign cube, one half plus one
half its maximum Fourier coefficient over odd-cardinality frequencies equals $1/4$.
\end{theorem}

\proofstep
  {FABL.BoundedCubeFunction}
  {context}
  {Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}
  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p121-b004}
\proofstep
  {FABL.instCoeFunBoundedCubeFunctionForallSignCubeReal}
  {context}
  {Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}
  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p121-b004}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $\varepsilon\in\mathbb R$, and let $f$ be a real-valued
function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube whose values lie in $[-1,1]$. The stable
influences of $f$ at noise parameter $1-\varepsilon$ are all at most $\varepsilon$ if
and only if, for every coordinate $i$, the sum over all subsets $S$ containing $i$ of
$(1-\varepsilon)^{|S|-1}$ times the square of the Fourier coefficient of $f$ at $S$ is
at most $\varepsilon$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Fourier coefficient square sum bound]
\lean{FABL.BoundedCubeFunction.sum_sq_fourierCoeff_le_one}
\label{FABL.BoundedCubeFunction.sum_sq_fourierCoeff_le_one}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BoundedCubeFunction, FABL.SignCube, FABL.fourierCoeff, FABL.parseval, FABL.uniformInner}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number and let $f$ be a real-valued function on the $n$-dimensional
sign cube whose values all lie in $[-1,1]$. The sum, over all subsets $S$ of the
coordinates, of the squares of the uniform Fourier coefficients of $f$ is at most $1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[A stable influence summand bound]
\lean{FABL.stableInfluence_term_le}
\label{FABL.stableInfluence_term_le}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.SignCube, FABL.fourierCoeff, FABL.stableInfluence}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f:\\{−1,1\\}^n\\to\\mathbb R$, and let $\\rho\\ge0$.
For any subset $S$ of the coordinates containing $i$, the summand $\\rho^{|S|-1}$ times
the square of the uniform Fourier coefficient of $f$ on $S$ is at most the stable
influence of $f$ at parameter $\\rho$ and coordinate $i$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Weighted Fourier coefficient bound]
\lean{FABL.hastad_weighted_fourierCoeff_le_sqrt}
\label{FABL.hastad_weighted_fourierCoeff_le_sqrt}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BoundedCubeFunction, FABL.HasSmallStableInfluences, FABL.fourierCoeff, FABL.stableInfluence, FABL.stableInfluence_term_le}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $\delta,\varepsilon\in[0,1]$ with
$\varepsilon\le\delta$, and let $f$ be a real-valued function on the $n$-dimensional
sign cube taking values in $[-1,1]$. Suppose every stable influence of $f$ at parameter
$\varepsilon$ is at most $\varepsilon$. For every subset $S$ of coordinates with odd
cardinality, $(1-\delta)^{|S|}\widehat f(S)\le\sqrt{\varepsilon}$, where $\widehat f(S)$
is the Fourier coefficient of $f$ at $S$.
\end{theorem}

  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p195-b001}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $0\leq\delta,\varepsilon\leq1$ with
$\varepsilon\leq\delta$, and let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to[-1,1]$. If every coordinate has stable
influence at most $\varepsilon$ at parameter $1-\varepsilon$, then the Håstad tester
acceptance probability at noise parameter $\delta$ is at most
$\frac12+\frac12\sqrt{\varepsilon}$.
\end{theorem}

Let $n$ be a natural number, let $\delta\in[0,1]$, and let $i$ be a coordinate in
$\mathrm{Fin}\,n$. The Håstad test with noise parameter $\delta$ accepts the Boolean
dictator on coordinate $i$, viewed as a function with values in $[-1,1]$, with
probability $1-\delta/2$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Bounds for a probability expectation]
\lean{FABL.pmfExpectation_mem_Icc_zero_one}
\label{FABL.pmfExpectation_mem_Icc_zero_one}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.pmfExpectation, FABL.pmfExpectation_const_one}
\difficulty{3}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite set, let $p$ be a probability mass function on $\Omega$, and
let $g:\Omega\to\bbr$ satisfy $0\le g(x)\le 1$ for every $x\in\Omega$. Then the
expectation of $g$ under $p$ lies in $[0,1]$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Bounds on randomized acceptance]
\lean{FABL.SignPredicate.randomizedValue_mem_Icc}
\label{FABL.SignPredicate.randomizedValue_mem_Icc}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.SignPredicate, FABL.SignPredicate.randomizedValue, FABL.pmfExpectation_mem_Icc_zero_one}
\difficulty{3}
Let $P$ be a Boolean predicate on finitely many signs and let each coordinate of $\mu$
lie in $[-1,1]$. The randomized acceptance value of $P$ at coordinate means $\mu$ lies
in $[0,1]$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Bounds on randomized check value]
\lean{FABL.SignQueryCheck.randomizedValue_mem_Icc}
\label{FABL.SignQueryCheck.randomizedValue_mem_Icc}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BoundedCubeFunction, FABL.SignPredicate.randomizedValue_mem_Icc, FABL.SignQueryCheck, FABL.SignQueryCheck.randomizedValue}
\difficulty{1}
Let $C$ be a sign query check and let $f$ be a real-valued function on the sign cube
taking values in $[-1,1]$. The randomized value of $C$ on $f$ lies in $[0,1]$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Bounds on tester acceptance probability]
\lean{FABL.SignTester.acceptanceProbability_mem_Icc}
\label{FABL.SignTester.acceptanceProbability_mem_Icc}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BoundedCubeFunction, FABL.SignQueryCheck.randomizedValue_mem_Icc, FABL.SignTester, FABL.SignTester.acceptanceProbability, FABL.pmfExpectation_mem_Icc_zero_one}
\difficulty{3}
Let $T$ be a sign tester with a finite seed space and let $f$ be a real-valued function
on the sign cube taking values in $[-1,1]$. The acceptance probability of $T$ on $f$
lies in $[0,1]$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Håstad soundness error]
\lean{FABL.hastadSoundnessError}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p195-b001}
\label{FABL.hastadSoundnessError}
\leanok
For real numbers $\mathrm{noise}$ and $\varepsilon$, define the soundness error to be
$\sqrt{\varepsilon}/2$ when $\varepsilon\leq\mathrm{noise}$, and $1/2$ otherwise.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Soundness error lies in the unit interval]
\lean{FABL.hastadSoundnessError_mem_Icc}
\label{FABL.hastadSoundnessError_mem_Icc}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.hastadSoundnessError}
\difficulty{4}
For all real numbers $\mathrm{noise}$ and $\varepsilon$, if $0\leq\varepsilon\leq1$,
then the soundness error—equal to $\sqrt{\varepsilon}/2$ when
$\varepsilon\leq\mathrm{noise}$ and to $1/2$ otherwise—lies in $[0,1]$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Vanishing soundness error]
\lean{FABL.hastadSoundnessError_tendsto_zero}
\label{FABL.hastadSoundnessError_tendsto_zero}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.hastadSoundnessError}
\difficulty{4}
For every noise level $r>0$, define $E_r(\varepsilon)=\sqrt{\varepsilon}/2$ when
$\varepsilon\le r$ and $E_r(\varepsilon)=1/2$ otherwise. Then $E_r(\varepsilon)\to 0$ as
$\varepsilon\to0$ through positive values.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Håstad dictator test family]
\lean{FABL.hastadDictatorTestFamily}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p194-b003}
\label{FABL.hastadDictatorTestFamily}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.SignTester, FABL.hastadTester}
Let $\delta$ be a real number with $0<\delta<1/2$, and let $n$ be a positive integer.
Define the test family member on the $n$-dimensional sign cube to be the Håstad tester
with parameter $2\delta$.
\end{definition}

  {FABL.hastadDictatorTestFamily}
  {context}
  {Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}
  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p194-b003,
    pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p194-b004}
For every $\delta\in(0,1/2)$, there is a family of finite-seed sign testers using
three-variable linear sign predicates, with thresholds $\alpha=1/2$ and
$\beta=1-\delta$, and error function $E_{2\delta}(\varepsilon)$, where
$E_r(\varepsilon)=\sqrt{\varepsilon}/2$ if $\varepsilon\le r$ and $1/2$ otherwise. The
predicate set is finite; the error maps $[0,1]$ into $[0,1]$ and tends to zero as
$\varepsilon$ approaches zero through positive values. Every test uses an allowed
predicate, every dictator is accepted with probability at least $\beta$, and every
function whose stable influences at parameters $(\varepsilon,\varepsilon)$ are all at
most $\varepsilon$ is accepted with probability at most
$\alpha+E_{2\delta}(\varepsilon)$, for every dimension, every positive dimension, and
every $\varepsilon\in[0,1]$.
\end{theorem}
